articles.summary: Here's how to watch this weekend's LSU vs. Louisiana Tech NCAAF game.
articles.body:
As LSU's contentious battle with the SEC continues, the team still has a regular schedule to stick to, and in Week 2 of the NCAAF season, they'll face Louisiana Tech at home in Tiger Stadium this Saturday night. While Louisiana Tech enter the game as underdogs, they're riding high on an 80-6 win against Northwestern State in Week 1. (And you thought LSU's 51-10 win over Clemson last weekend was brutal…)

Here's what you need to know to watch the LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game, and take a look at the complete NCAAF schedule for Week 2.

Streaming: SECN+ , ESPN Unlimited, YouTube TV, Fubo, DIRECTV and more

When is the LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game?

LSU and Louisiana Tech play on Saturday, Sept. 12 at 7:30 p.m. ET.

What channel is the LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game on?

The LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game will air on SEC Network+. (SECN+ is complementary to SEC Network and part of your subscription with your cable, satellite, or streaming provider. Games on SECN+ are is only available digitally through ESPN Unlimited or by using a laptop, tablet or smartphone and authenticating with your cable login credentials if you have a plan that includes the SEC Network.)

How to watch LSU vs. Louisiana Tech without cable:

Saturday's LSU vs. Louisiana Tech game will stream on SECN+ which is included as part of ESPN Unlimited. ESPN Unlimited is included on live TV platforms like YouTube TV, Fubo, and DirecTV.

articles.title: Falcons Draft 2027: Way-Too-Early 2027 NFL Mock Draft 1.0
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons are in dire straits heading into the first week of the 2026 NFL season, as both projected starters at the quarterback position are out fo...
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are in dire straits heading into the first week of the 2026 NFL season, as both projected starters at the quarterback position are out for the first game against the Pittsburgh Steelers . But that's not why we're here. Draft season is year-round nowadays, and the Falcons need multiple players throughout the roster if they're going to build a sturdy foundation to start competing for the division/conference sooner rather than later. Atlanta has done a great job not overextending in the short term, owning the most cap space in 2027, despite extending Drake London , Bijan Robinson , Kyle Pitts and Matthew Bergeron this offseason. However, even with the potential depth that money can bring, general manager Ian Cunningham and President Matt Ryan have to hit on the draft. So, we're going to get a jump on next year's draft by pinpointing seven picks in this way-too-early 2027 NFL mock draft.

Round 1, Pick 6: Darian Mensah, QB, Miami

I'm buying into the hype early. The former Duke transfer has come out of the gate firing, albeit against Stanford and Florida A&M. Mensah's 91.1% completion percentage is the second-best start to a college football season for any quarterback with 40+ attempts in the first two games, while his 271.7 Passer Efficiency Rating is the best. 41-of-45 for 653 yards, eight touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Miami is looking to run through the ACC with ease, and hopefully, that means we see plenty of NFL-caliber throws from Mensah that will make him the next transfer quarterback who impresses scouts this season.

Round 2, Pick 38: Samson Okunlola, OT, Miami

To build the future, you have to fortify the foundation, and that means Atlanta has to acquire a left tackle, so Jake Matthews can be the family man he deserves to be. Samson Okunlola's movement skills, especially his absurdly quick feet, are just one of his impressive traits that scouts will bet on if he comes out after this season. Okunlola's 6'6", 330-pound frame gives him such impressive size and he has experience playing inside as well.

Round 3, Pick 70: Tavion Gadson, DT, Kentucky

With Brandon Dorlus heading to the edge, the Falcons lose the interior pressure that Dorlus and, to a lesser extent, Ruke Orhorhoro brought on opposing quarterbacks. Tavion Gadson immediately brings that pass-rush juice back to the Falcons' line along with a knack for using his athleticism and size (6'4", 302 pounds) to stuff up the A-gaps.

Round 4, Pick 105: Niki Prongos, OT, Stanford

I couldn't help myself, and if Cunningham and Stefanski were met with the same choice, I don't think they would help themselves either. Niki Prongos hadn't started playing football until his senior year of high school, choosing to play baseball and basketball instead. Even in high school, he played tight end and defensive tackle alongside his duties at tackle. Prongos is such a fun athlete and would be a stellar pickup for Bill Callahan.

Round 5, Pick 179: Bruce Mitchell, C, BYU

#63 in white and blue has a case to be the best center in college football, and it would not surprise me if he finds a way into day two when it's all said and done. Mitchell has a stout anchor in pass protection alongside some strong hands in the run game. With this move, the Falcons would solve all three of their "problems" along the offensive line in one draft.

Round 6, Pick 216: Fluff Bothwell, RB, Mississippi State

Brian Robinson Jr. feels like a rental for this season, but the future of backing up Bijan Robinson can look like a running back like Fluff Bothwell. Don't let the name fool you; there is absolutely nothing soft about his game. Bothwell is 5'10", 230 pounds and, for a man of that size, he has impressive agility.

Round 7, Pick 220: Duce Robinson, WR, Florida State

KJ Duff is one of those players in the 2027 draft you wish had transferred to another team so he could get more eyes on his performance with a quarterback who can get him the ball. The same goes for Florida State receiver Duce Robinson. Robinson is 6'6", 230 pounds and has an incredibly large catch radius, while allowing Drake London to work more in the slot and Kyle Pitts over the middle of the field.

The 2026/2027 football season has kicked off, but week 1 isn't over without a little Sunday Night Football action. As it turns out, most NFL games are played on Sunday, and after a summer off from tailgating and Fantasy Football chats, this weekend's games are highly anticipated. On Sunday, September 13, catch games from the Kansas City Chiefs , Philadelphia Eagles , and more, and tune in for the first Sunday Night Football game of the season when the Dallas Cowboys and New York Giants attempt to win their first game of the season.

A lot of football is played on Sundays throughout the NFL season, but there's usually only one Sunday Night Football Game. The official time slot for Sunday Night Football game is 5:20 p.m. PT/8:20 ET , with teams alternating week to week. In the 2026/2027 season, there will be two Sunday Night Football games on November 26 (week 12): The Chiefs vs. Bills at 5:20 p.m. PT/8:20 ET and the Patriots vs. Chargers at 5:20 p.m. PT/8:20 ET.

Although it doesn't have any free trials, it's the cheapest way to watch Sunday Night Football, with a Sling 1 Day pass available for $4.99, a Sling 3 Day pass option for $9.99, or a full subscription starting at $45.99 per month. An even better option is the Sling Essentials & Select bundle ($34.99) which includes FOX News, ESPN, FS1, NFL Network, plus add on Sports Extra for access to NFL RedZone, FS2, SEC, ACC and more. If you're a mega-mega fan, consider the Season Pass bundle ($199+) which includes five months of Sling Essentials & Select + Sports Extra (which includes RedZone, ESPN channels, and NCAA conference networks like SEC, ACC, and Big Ten. Plus FOX One app access).

Fubo has a free seven-day trial period before your selected plan (starting at $84.99) kicks in. articles.title: A.J. Brown Said Seahawks 'Cannot F--k With' Patriots WRs in Trending Sideline Video from Week 1
articles.summary: A.J. Brown was confident in the ability of the New England Patriots' receivers to beat the Seattle Seahawks' secondary in New England's 13-10 loss to Seattle on Wednesday.
articles.body:
A.J. Brown was confident in the ability of the New England Patriots' receivers to beat the Seattle Seahawks' secondary in New England's 13-10 loss to Seattle on Wednesday.

"If y'all boys just could hold up, we gonna score this s--t," Brown told the Patriots' offensive linemen during the game in a video released by the team. "They cannot f--k with none of us at wide receiver, I'm telling you. We running wide open, you hear me?"

Brown caught three of his four targets for 26 yards against the Seahawks before exiting the game in the third quarter due to an ankle injury .

New England eventually placed him on injured reserve Friday, meaning that he'll miss at least four games before he can return.

On the same drive that Brown suffered the injury against Seattle, the Patriots kicked a field goal to take a 10-0 lead in the Super Bowl LX rematch.

While the Seahawks were without starting quarterback Sam Darnold since their opening drive of the game due to a hip injury , they were able to swing momentum in their favor throughout the rest of the game.

Seattle scored 13 consecutive points to jump in front, as New England's offense struggled without Brown.

The four Patriots drives after his injury ended with a punt and three interceptions by quarterback Drake Maye. His final interception came with New England in field-goal range as just under 30 seconds remained in the fourth quarter, sealing the final result.

Maye was sacked three times in the game after he was sacked on six occasions during the Patriots' Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks last season.

Outside of Brown, Mack Hollins was the only New England wide receiver to surpass 20 yards in Wednesday's defeat.

articles.title: Travis Kelce made unusual $35,000 decision as Eighty-Seven and Running faced questions over its operations
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s latest charitable decision has drawn attention for a reason that goes beyond the money involved. In January 2026, the Kansas City Chief.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s latest charitable decision has drawn attention for a reason that goes beyond the money involved. In January 2026, the Kansas City Chiefs star chose not to send his latest $35,000 charity prize to his own foundation. Instead, he directed it to a Kansas City nonprofit he has supported for years, a move that comes as questions surround the governance and financial reporting of his organization.Travis Kelce sends $35,000 prize to established Kansas City nonprofitKelce earned the money after winning the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Charity Challenge for the third time on January 7, 2026. Unlike his previous victories in 2020 and 2024, however, the prize will not benefit his Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation.The funds are going to Operation Breakthrough, a long-standing Kansas City organization that works with children, teenagers and families. Kelce has previously supported the nonprofit through his foundation’s partnership with its Ignition Lab, a program focused on workforce development for teens.The choice also comes shortly after Taylor Swift donated $250,000 to Operation Breakthrough, adding another high-profile connection to the organization.Kelce’s decision stands out because it breaks from his own recent pattern. Rather than keeping the award money within a foundation he established, he opted for an organization with an established structure and track record.CharityWatch CEO and executive director Laurie Styron viewed that decision positively.“As for Kelce’s decision to donate his contest winnings to an established charity, in the short term this was the right call,” said CharityWatch CEO and executive director Laurie Styron in her interview with The Arizona Republic. “The people operating the foundation need time to get their accounting, governance, and legal house in order. It was the responsible move under the circumstances.”Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation faces questions over its operationsThe timing of Kelce’s decision is important. His Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation, which he launched in 2015, has come under scrutiny following a review of its federal tax filings by The Arizona Republic.The reporting raised questions about the foundation’s spending and internal structure. Over a three-year period, the organization reportedly spent about 41 cents of every dollar on charitable activities. It also paid hundreds of thousands of dollars to A&A Management Group, a company co-founded by Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and André Eanes.The foundation has also reportedly operated with only two board members and without several standard officer positions, including a president and secretary.Styron raised concerns about the relationship between the charity and the management company.“It appears to function more as an extension of the management company versus as an independent public charity,” Styron said after reviewing the filings. “That’s not how charities work. It’s wrong.”The foundation has disputed the implication that its spending figures tell the full story. Aaron Eanes, its executive director, said expenses connected to charitable work had been incorrectly classified as management costs on IRS filings for nearly a decade.According to Eanes, the organization has been correcting those filings. He also said management fees fell sharply in 2024 and reached zero in 2025, while plans are underway to expand the board and strengthen reporting.He stated that the organization is “dedicated to ensuring this foundation operates at the highest standards,” according to The Arizona Republic.Kelce’s move therefore carries significance beyond one $35,000 award. It highlights how athlete-led charities can face intense scrutiny once their public profile grows, and why financial transparency and independent oversight matter just as much as charitable intentions.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New Lamar Jackson Rumors Update Ravens Contract Extension Buzz Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson won't sign a last-minute contract extension with the Baltimore Ravens before the team's 2026 season begins on Sunday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson won't sign a last-minute contract extension with the Baltimore Ravens before the team's 2026 season begins on Sunday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Jackson has been "reluctant" to negotiate a long-term extension "for whatever reason" despite the Ravens being willing to make him the highest-paid quarterback in the NFL, per Schefter .

Jackson is currently under contract through 2027.

However, it's understandable that the Ravens may be motivated to finalize a new deal at the end of this year in order to avoid his $84.3 million cap hit during the 2027 season (via Spotrac ).

Schefter also reported Saturday that "no deal is expected anytime soon," though.

Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta previously said that he was "optimistic" about reaching a contract extension agreement with Jackson on Sept. 2, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley .

Despite the lack of an extension, a change of scenery for the two-time MVP doesn't appear to be on the horizon.

On Saturday, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic reported that the relationship between Jackson and the Ravens is the "healthiest it's been" while both sides have "every intention of continuing their work together for years to come."

Jackson has spent all eight seasons of his career in Baltimore, establishing himself as one of the league's top quarterbacks.

While injuries limited him to 13 games in 2025, he still completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 2,549 yards and 21 touchdowns compared to seven interceptions. He also rushed for 349 yards and two scores.

Jackson and the Ravens will face the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Inspiring story on balancing motherhood and career:“You can achieve anything. You can be a part of anything that you want to”-How Brittany Mahomes continues to inspire her children
articles.summary: NFL News: For Brittany Mahomes, motherhood did not mean putting her own ambitions on hold. Instead, becoming a mother of three appears to have changed the way s.
articles.body: For Brittany Mahomes, motherhood did not mean putting her own ambitions on hold. Instead, becoming a mother of three appears to have changed the way she approaches both family and work. The wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes says her children have given her a stronger sense of purpose, while also pushing her to show them what it means to dream big and work hard.How motherhood changed Brittany Mahomes’ outlook on lifeBrittany Mahomes entered motherhood while already building a life of her own. She had a background in soccer, fitness and business, while her relationship with Patrick Mahomes placed her close to the intense world of professional football.Then came a new role that changed everything.Brittany and Patrick welcomed their first child, daughter Sterling, in 2021. Their family grew again with the arrival of son Bronze in 2022 and daughter Golden in 2025.Three children later, Brittany says motherhood has changed more than her daily routine. It has influenced the way she thinks about her goals, her time and the example she wants to set at home.“Being a mom changed so many things in my life and changed how I looked at so many things,” Brittany, 30, told Yahoo Entertainment in June 2026. “It really reshaped and redefined a lot of things in my life.”That change does not sound like a retreat from ambition. If anything, Brittany appears to have found another reason to keep moving.She explained that motherhood has made her more deliberate about the opportunities she takes and the people and causes she gives her attention to. Her priorities have become clearer, with family now playing a major role in how she measures what is worth pursuing.That shift is especially meaningful for someone whose life has long been lived in the public eye.Brittany Mahomes wants her children to dream without limitsOne of the strongest themes in Brittany’s recent comments is the importance of showing her children that their dreams should not come with unnecessary limits.“It’s made me more intentional, more purposeful and, honestly, more motivated to keep going and keep showing my kids that there are no boundaries in front of you. You can achieve anything. You can be a part of anything that you want to. You need to dream big and understand that you have to work hard and do the hard things to do the fun things.”There is a simple lesson behind those words. Brittany does not want her children to learn about ambition only through their father’s NFL career. She wants them to see it through her actions, too.That means continuing to build her own professional identity while raising three young children.For Brittany, success is not just about having a busy schedule or being attached to a famous sports family. It is about demonstrating that family and personal ambition can exist at the same time.That message becomes even more powerful because her children are growing up around two parents with demanding careers.Brittany Mahomes wants her children to see both parents work hardPatrick Mahomes has spent much of his adult life under the brightest lights in American sports. His NFL career demands long hours, travel, preparation and an enormous physical commitment.Brittany understands that her children see that effort.But she also wants them to see hers.“At the end of the day, my kids are watching me, and I want them to know that I’m working hard,” she told Yahoo!Life in February 2024. “I’m out here doing things as well, because they noticed their dad’s gone all the time. And he’s working hard and doing stuff that he loves. So, I want them to see both of us going out and conquering the world.”That perspective gives her story a more personal edge. Brittany is not simply trying to fit a career around motherhood. She is thinking about what her children will learn by watching her navigate both.Her message is also about balance. Children may see the finished result of a parent’s work, but they rarely see everything that happens before it.Brittany wants her children to understand that achievement requires effort, patience and a willingness to take on difficult moments.Brittany Mahomes is learning when to say noMotherhood has also changed the way Brittany views her time.“I think when you become a mom, you learn to say no to things that aren’t as important and focus on what’s best for your life and your family,” she said.It is a particularly relatable part of her story.A larger career can bring more invitations, projects and opportunities. Yet having children can force a person to decide which ones truly matter.For Brittany, that appears to have created a clearer filter. Instead of trying to do everything, she wants to focus on things that align with her values and the example she hopes to give her children.That does not mean ambition has disappeared. It means the definition of ambition has changed.Her goals now sit alongside school days, family moments, parenting responsibilities and the realities of raising three children while living under constant public attention.Brittany Mahomes is building a legacy beyond Patrick MahomesBrittany will always be closely connected to Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. Their marriage, family and shared life have naturally made them one of the NFL’s most recognizable couples.Yet her story has increasingly moved beyond that connection.Her soccer background helped shape her interest in sports. Her fitness work gave her an independent professional identity. Her involvement in women’s soccer has also allowed her to participate in the growth of the sport from a different side of the field.Now, motherhood has added another layer to that journey.Rather than viewing her role as a choice between being a mother and pursuing her own goals, Brittany appears determined to show her children that both can have a place in the same life.Her approach is not about pretending that balancing everything is easy. It is about understanding what deserves her energy.And perhaps that is the most inspiring part of her story.Brittany Mahomes is not telling her children to dream big simply because she wants them to succeed. She is trying to show them what that looks like by continuing to dream, work and build while being present for the family she has created.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New NFL Rumors Update Parker Washington, Jaguars Contract Buzz After Michael Wilson, Cardinals Deal
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington is reportedly on track to start the 2026 season on an expiring contract.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington is reportedly on track to start the 2026 season on an expiring contract.

NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe reported Saturday it is "unlikely" Washington will sign an extension before the Jaguars open the season Sunday afternoon.

According to Wolfe, the Jaguars previously "explored" a deal in the range of the three-year, $75 million extension Michael Wilson recently signed with the Arizona Cardinals.

Wilson signed his deal, which included $47 million in guaranteed money, after topping 1,000 receiving yards in 17 games of his third season with the Cardinals.

Washington is currently heading into the 2026 season under a $3.7 million cap hit in the final year of his rookie deal .

He told reporters that as of Thursday he was still getting daily updates from his agent about ongoing communication with the Jaguars.

The Jaguars wide receiver also said he felt his job was "to come out here and stay ready to go and just do my job."

Washington recorded 847 receiving yards in 16 games during his own third NFL season.

Most of his production came down the stretch of the campaign. He made 22 catches on 32 targets for 400 receiving yards and two touchdowns in the final four games of the Jags' push for the playoffs.

Washington was rewarded in the Wild Card round with a team-high 12 targets, of which he caught seven for 107 receiving yards and a touchdown before the Jaguars were eliminated by the Buffalo Bills.

ESPN's Michael DiRocco reported last month that Washington had earned his spot as the Jaguars' WR1 after working as Trevor Lawrence's "favorite target" in training camp.

Regardless of the wide receiver's contract status, the Jaguars will hope Lawrence and Washington are able to continue building on that connection when kicking off the season Sunday at 1 p.m. ET against the visiting Cleveland Browns.

articles.title: San Diego State's offense can't match defense's performance in loss to UCLA
articles.summary: Despite the defense largely holding UCLA’s offense in check, SDSU’s offense managed just 189 yards and one touchdown in a 28-10 loss.
articles.body:
PASADENA -- San Diego State 's defense did practically everything they could to keep the Aztecs in the game against UCLA . They just needed the offense to come along for the ride.

Despite the defense largely holding UCLA's offense in check, SDSU's offense managed just 189 yards and one touchdown — coming effectively in garbage time — in a 28-10 loss to the Bruins at the Rose Bowl on Saturday.

"Inefficiency on offense led to a bunch of snaps for the defense," head coach Sean Lewis said. "Starting three and out there constantly, we were behind in the field position game. So I think just the culmination of snaps, the inefficiency on offense. It starts with the play calling, with myself, the leadership throughout the course of the week, so that we can have more success and flip the field."

Nowhere was SDSU's offensive struggle more apparent than in the passing game. The Aztecs completed just six passes for 45 yards, and several deep shots by quarterback Jayden Denegal were wildly off-target.

"[We] felt like we had good matchups on the edge," Lewis said. "There was a lot of single-high coverage. Again, those are good, calculated shots downrange. We got balls on hands that we didn't catch. We had other guys wide open that we missed."

San Diego State held up defensively for the majority of the game. They kept UCLA scoreless in the first half and limited them to just seven points through three quarters.

"I think we did a good job with our aggression," said sophomore cornerback Mike Lindsay, who intercepted UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava in the second quarter. "I think that caught them by surprise. I think that they're thinking we were going to be a little bit weaker than how we came out there, and we did a good job stopping the run and containing [Iamaleava] because he likes his ground, he likes to run around, but we kept him in the pocket [and] kept him on the ground."

Despite the defense's containment of UCLA's offense, SDSU's own unit generated even less. They failed to score in the first three quarters and managed their only touchdown with 2:28 remaining in the fourth.

"We knew how to scheme up and get our guys in the right spot," sophomore offensive lineman Michael Watkins said. "I think it was just blocking in the moment. You know, it was just the little letups … it would be [blowing off] technique and it would let up."

Eventually, the defense collapsed under the weight of the pressure. As Lewis noted, having the defense on the field for as long as they were led to exhaustion. UCLA won the time-of-possession battle by nearly 10 minutes, and SDSU ran out of gas, allowing three rushing touchdowns in the fourth quarter for a final result that was closer than the score indicated.

"Good teams are able to play balanced and use special teams as a weapon to flip the field," Lewis said. "So when you got two out of three phases doing well, you've got to evaluate and assess what's going on with that other phase as you go forward with it."

The Aztecs' next attempt to produce a more balanced performance will take place at home, against James Madison at 7 p.m. on Sept. 19. Despite Saturday's difficult results, Watkins expressed optimism that his group is capable of a stronger outcome.

"We just know what we can do, and we know we can keep punching them in the mouth, and we know how it feels like," he said. "You know, we [weren't] finishing, we [weren't] getting the end zone, but the way we [were] coming off the field, it felt like we're [really] close. We just gotta get it in."

articles.title: Harrisburg beats O’Gorman by one in 48th Dakota Bowl
articles.summary: SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — A missed extra point was the difference between #3 O’Gorman and #5 Harrisburg in the 48th annual Bob Burns Dakota Bowl, and this y...
articles.body:
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — A missed extra point was the difference between #3 O'Gorman and #5 Harrisburg in the 48th annual Bob Burns Dakota Bowl, and this year the visiting Tigers will head back home with the win, 21-20.

O'Gorman scored on their first drive of the ballgame, a long sustained push capped off with a short rushing touchdown, but from there the offense went stagnant the rest of the first half.

Harrisburg had a nice, long drive of their own capped off with a QB sneak from Jonah Young to tie things up, a pick six for Bryson Esser gave the Tigers a lead heading into the locker room as well.

Out of the break, O'Gorman's offense re-found its rhythm and capped a six minute drive with a Brady Majeres rushing touchdown to tie the game at 14.

Harrisburg would march down and score to retake a touchdown lead, but the Knights responded this time, hitting paydirt for the six, unfortunately for them, a strong Harrisburg push on the line caused enough pressure to force a miss and the Tigers led by one, 21-20.

The Knights had a chance in the final minute as they got the ball with 53 seconds left, but an untimely fumble, recovered by Harrisburg marked the end of the game.

O'Gorman moves to 1-2 after the loss while Harrisburg is 2-1.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith Predicted to Pair With $29 Million WR Star in NFL Draft
articles.summary: Ohio State superstar WR projected to land in NFC East. The post Jeremiah Smith Predicted to Pair With $29 Million WR Star in NFL Draft appeared first on HEAV...
articles.body:
The New York Giants may already have Malik Nabers returning to their offense, but one 2027 NFL mock draft has them adding an even bigger prize alongside him.

Athlon Sports' Luke Easterling projected the Giants to select Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith with the No. 3 overall pick in his updated mock draft after Week 1 of the college football season.

For Jaxson Dart , it would potentially give him one of the NFL's most dangerous young receiving duos.

Giants Predicted to Draft Jeremiah Smith No. 3

"It looks like Malik Nabers is on track to return in Week 1 after missing most of last season with a knee injury, but even with him at full strength and the addition of third-rounder Malachi Fields , the Giants would still be wise not to pass on the chance to land Smith," Easterling wrote.

"The best overall player in this entire class, Smith is one of the best receiver prospects I've ever evaluated, and would instantly make this one of the most talented pass-catching groups in the NFL."

That is a massive statement considering the talent expected to be available in the 2027 draft.

Easterling still has Smith going behind Texas quarterback Arch Manning and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore . If New York were sitting at No. 3, though, he believes the Giants should take the best overall player rather than force another position.

The Ohio State star entered his junior season with 163 catches for 2,558 yards and 27 touchdowns over his first two years. He then opened 2026 with eight catches for 151 yards and two touchdowns in a 56-3 win over Ball State.

That moved him to 171 career receptions, 2,709 yards and 29 touchdowns after only one game of his junior season.

Jeremiah Smith Could Give Jaxson Dart Elite Giants Duo

The Giants selected Nabers No. 6 overall in 2024 and signed him to a four-year, $29.2 million fully guaranteed rookie contract.

He immediately looked like a franchise receiver, catching 109 passes for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns as a rookie. His second season ended after only four games when he suffered a torn ACL.

Nabers practiced fully throughout this week but was listed as questionable for Sunday's opener against the Dallas Cowboys .

Pairing him with Smith would give Dart two young receivers who were each viewed as elite prospects before reaching the NFL.

"Giving a young quarterback like Jaxson Dart a trio like that would be a massive win for the Giants' future," Easterling wrote, also including Fields in the group.

Dart gave New York reasons to keep building around him during his rookie year.

The 2025 first-round pick started 12 games and completed 63.7% of his passes for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions. He added 487 rushing yards and nine scores, giving him 24 total touchdowns.

His biggest limitation was that he barely got to play with Nabers, who appeared in only four games before the knee injury ended his season.

New York spent the offseason adding help, including Fields in the third round, but Easterling doesn't believe that should stop the Giants from taking Smith if the opportunity comes.

It's far too early to know whether New York will actually pick anywhere near No. 3.

But if the Giants do land that high in the 2027 draft, Easterling's prediction would put arguably the class' best overall player opposite their $29 million star and give Dart an entirely different level of firepower.

articles.title: Ferrum falls in overtime thriller
articles.summary: DURHAM, N.C.(WFXR) — Ferrum College rallied from a 19-7 second-quarter deficit to take a late fourth-quarter lead, but Shaw University forced overtime and ed...
articles.body:
DURHAM, N.C.(WFXR) -- Ferrum College rallied from a 19-7 second-quarter deficit to take a late fourth-quarter lead, but Shaw University forced overtime and edged the Panthers, 34-28, Saturday afternoon in non-conference football action at Durham County Memorial Stadium.

Ferrum took a 28-25 lead with 1:10 remaining when

on a 17-yard touchdown pass. Shaw answered with a 33-yard field goal as time expired to force overtime, then scored on a 3-yard touchdown run by Alexander Marsh to claim the win.

THE BASICS Shaw jumped out to a 13-0 lead in the opening quarter on a 58-yard touchdown run by Fabian Diggs and a 5-yard touchdown pass from Alexander Marsh to Antrel Gibson.

Ferrum answered early in the second quarter when Foutz scored on a 1-yard touchdown run, capping a 10-play, 47-yard drive. Shaw responded with a 34-yard touchdown pass from Marsh to Reggie King Jr., but Ferrum closed the half with another scoring drive, as Foutz found Gray for a 30-yard touchdown to cut the deficit to 19-14 at the break.

The Panthers took their first lead of the afternoon early in the third quarter when Foutz scored on another 1-yard touchdown run, putting Ferrum ahead 21-19. Shaw regained the lead two minutes later on Marsh's 22-yard touchdown pass to Rashid Jones.

Ferrum's defense kept the Panthers within striking distance, and Ferrum rallied again in the fourth quarter. Foutz and Gray connected for their second touchdown of the game, this time on a 17-yard scoring pass that capped a nine-play, 81-yard drive and put the Panthers ahead 28-25 with 1:10 remaining.

Shaw then drove 58 yards in the final 1:10 and tied the game on Benjamin Turner's 33-yard field goal as time expired. Ferrum had the ball first in overtime, buit failed to score. Shaw took possession first and finished a six-play, 25-yard drive with Marsh's three-yard touchdown run to secure the victory.

KEY STATS Ferrum: Foutz completed 14 of 27 passes for 166 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 26 yards and two touchdowns;

rushed 20 times for 135 yards; Gray caught eight passes for 111 yards and two touchdowns and added 63 punt-return yards and 66 kickoff-return yards for 240 all-purpose yards;

had two receptions for 17 yards. Defensively

led the Panthers with eight tackles, including two tackles for loss.

Shaw: Marsh completed 18 of 29 passes for 287 yards and three touchdowns and rushed for 17 yards and a touchdown; Diggs rushed 19 times for 178 yards and a touchdown; King Jr. caught three passes for 103 yards and a touchdown; and Jones had two receptions for 38 yards and a touchdown.
